title: DecryptionKey and SigningKey are traits, not concrete key types
description: smime-tree does not accept a private key material directly. The API takes &dyn DecryptionKey and &dyn SigningKey, which the caller implements. The crate provides the CEK decrypt_cek() and sign() signatures but does not know whether the key is in memory, an HSM, a PKCS#11 token, or a remote KMS. A future contributor might suggest adding a concrete in-memory key type to 'make it easier to get started'. That would be a trap: any concrete key type hard-codes an assumption about where the key lives. The trait boundary is the correct design because it allows the same S/MIME logic to be used regardless of key storage, which is a core requirement for an S/MIME library used in server contexts.
